question.question:
Consider a fictional token whose circulating supply stands at 190 million tokens. A monitoring desk is reviewing three addresses. Address A has a balance of 1000000 tokens and sent 20000 tokens out during the last 24 hours. Address B has a balance of 1900000 tokens and sent 550000 tokens out. Address C has a balance of 2000000 tokens and sent nothing out. Under the desk's rule, an address is flagged as a whale when its balance is strictly greater than 3 percent of circulating supply, or when its 24-hour outflow is strictly greater than 600000 tokens; a balance or outflow that exactly matches its threshold does not count. An address tagged as an exchange cold wallet can never be a whale, whatever its balance or outflow; this cold-wallet tag is assigned to address none (none means no address carries the tag). The whale share of supply is defined as the total balance of every flagged address divided by circulating supply, stated in percent. What is the whale share of supply in percent?

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `percent` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Balance level in tokens an address must strictly exceed to qualify by balance
Number of addresses flagged as whales after the cold-wallet exclusion
Combined token balance of all flagged whale addresses
